reason: E1 describes a nano-bridged honeycomb structure with dislocation highways in a two-phase (fcc + B2) alloy, not an initially single-phase HEA, so the key premise of such channels existing in a single-phase state is unsupported. E2 discusses ductility mechanisms in BCC RHEAs but provides no evidence for stress/temperature-induced intermetallic precipitation or its effect on dislocation channels. The cited evidence does not support the core mechanistic claims.
premises: Nano-bridged dislocation channels exist in single-phase HEAs and provide efficient dislocation highways for crack blunting
Stress- or temperature-induced phase transformation can form discrete intermetallic precipitates in initially single-phase HEAs
These precipitates form at critical locations such as former dislocation channels or grain boundaries
Precipitates disrupt the nano-bridged dislocation channels, impeding dislocation mobility and crack-tip blunting
This disruption causes a measurable reduction in fracture toughness compared to the pristine single-phase state
